basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost at its Braga plant and put the improvements in place?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish conversion cost per part at the Braga plant and size the improvements that could lower it.

gate.label: Initiatives go/no-go
gate.decision: Which sized initiatives go into implementation at the plant, and which stop here?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Put the agreed improvements in place at the plant and show their effect on conversion cost per part.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the results against the baseline and the handover to the plant team?

workstreams.name: Conversion cost baseline
workstreams.answers: What is conversion cost per part at the Braga plant today, and where does it build up?
activities: Calculate conversion cost per part from operational data
Observe lines on the floor and record where losses occur
Interview the people who run the lines about cost drivers

workstreams.name: Cost improvement sizing
workstreams.answers: Which improvements can lower conversion cost per part by a measurable amount, and what is each worth?
activities: Identify candidate improvements from the losses found
Size each improvement's effect on cost per part from data
Prepare the sized improvement list for the go/no-go decision

workstreams.name: Improvement implementation
workstreams.answers: How are the chosen improvements put in place at the Braga plant, and in what order?
activities: Detail each chosen improvement and set the order of changes
Prepare the changes with the people who run the lines
Put the changes into operation after the steering workshop

workstreams.name: Cost per part tracking
workstreams.answers: Do the improvements keep running, and does cost per part fall against the baseline?
activities: Set up a tracker of cost per part against the baseline
Check that each improvement keeps running on the floor
Compare operational data on cost per part with the baseline

workstreams.name: Plant team capability
workstreams.answers: Can the Braga plant team run the improvements and keep them going after handover?
activities: Train the plant team on the changed ways of working
Coach the plant team as they run the changes themselves
Document who owns each improvement for the handover

deliverables.name: Line loss observations and cost driver findings
Conversion cost per part baseline for the Braga plant
Sized improvement list with baseline for go/no-go
Cost per part tracker against the baseline
Results and handover pack against the baseline
Improvement ownership register for the handover

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Agree access to plant data and people
events.decision: Will the plant give the team its cost data and access to line staff from week 1?
agenda: Present the Diagnostic objective and the weeks 1 to 5 steps
Discuss the plant data and line access the evidence work needs
Confirm who gives the team access to data and people at the plant

events.label: Check-in: baseline findings
events.purpose: Review line losses and the cost baseline
events.decision: Which cost drivers from the findings should the sizing cover in weeks 4 and 5?
agenda: Review line loss observations and cost driver findings
Review the conversion cost per part baseline for the Braga plant
Discuss which cost drivers the sizing should cover next

events.label: Initiatives go/no-go
events.decision: Which sized initiatives go into implementation at the plant, and which stop here?
agenda: Present the sized improvement list with baseline for go/no-go
Review the line loss findings and the cost per part baseline
Decide which initiatives go into implementation and which stop

events.label: Workshop: go-live readiness
events.decision: Which improvements are ready to go live at the plant, and which wait?
agenda: Review the improvement detail and change sequence for each improvement
Review the cost per part tracker and how results will be read
Decide which improvements are ready to go live and which wait

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Close out results and plant handover
events.decision: Approve the results against the baseline and the handover to the plant team?
agenda: Present the results and handover pack against the baseline
Review the go-live record, training materials and ownership register
Decide on approval of the results and the handover to the plant team

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; the 13 to 16 weeks are an estimate to confirm before this plan becomes a quote.
Implementation takes the middle of its 8 to 12 week estimate; savings slow to show in the cost data would push it to 12.
No Measurement phase: tracking against the baseline stays inside Implementation; confirm whether the client wants tracking after the engagement ends.

sub_questions.question: What is conversion cost per part at the Braga plant today, and where does it build up?
Which improvements can lower conversion cost per part by a measurable amount, and how much is each worth?
How are the chosen improvements put in place at the plant, and in what order?
Do the improvements keep running at the plant, and does cost per part fall against the baseline?

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phases.why: One plant, so one site diagnosed on the floor; interviews run alongside. Estimate sits inside the archetype's typical 3 to 6 weeks.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data

phases.why: The single plant is the pilot site; no rollout wave is needed. Estimate sits inside the archetype's typical 8 to 16 weeks.

sizing.levers: Carry only the largest sized improvements into Implementation, which holds most of the weeks; running changes side by side would also shorten it.
